errata.orig:
BEGIN:VCALENDAR
   CALSCALE:GREGORIAN
   PRODID:-//Example Inc.//Example Calendar//EN
   VERSION:2.0
   BEGIN:VEVENT
   DTSTAMP:20080205T191224Z
   DTSTART:20081006
   SUMMARY:Planning meeting
   UID:4088E990AD89CB3DBB484909
   END:VEVENT
   END:VCALENDAR
errata.correct:
BEGIN:VCALENDAR
   CALSCALE:GREGORIAN
   PRODID:-//Example Inc.//Example Calendar//EN
   VERSION:2.0
   BEGIN:VEVENT
   DTSTAMP:20080205T191224Z
   DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20081006
   SUMMARY:Planning meeting
   UID:4088E990AD89CB3DBB484909
   END:VEVENT
   END:VCALENDAR
errata.notes:
The default value type of DTSTART is DATE-TIME. The definition of DATE-TIME makes the time portion mandatory. By declaring the value type explicitly, this solution makes the value legal and matches the xCal sample in B.1.2

Another solution is to change the property value to match the default DATE-TIME type
    DTSTART:20081006T191224Z
and adjust the xCal example in B.1.2 to match
        <dtstart>
          <date-time>2008-10-06T19:12:24Z</date-time>
        </dtstart>

This has been reported before here: https://errata.rfc-editor.org/eid3315/
This provides a suggestion on how to solve this.

I believe this is a correction, consistent with the standard. The argumentation below:

Context: The RFC defines `pattern-date` and `value-date` , `pattern-date-time` and `value-date-time`.

(1) The RFC has a consistency: Each tag identifies the one pattern for the data and with that allows a single data type in the programming language to be mapped.
Patterns are either used once or in case of `value-period`, the tag <end> and <start> imply a single pattern `pattern-date-time`.

(2) Implementing this for Python, "value-date | value-date-time" creates a consistent code base with type selection based on the tag. Using `pattern-date | pattern-date-time` requires selection of the type based on the text's content (either date or date-time). That would make UNTIL the only place that does that in RFC6321.

[RPC] Note to Verifier: Please consider whether adjustments are needed for https://errata.rfc-editor.org/eid3315/. For example, if this erratum is verified, perhaps EID 3315 should be deleted or reclassified as "Rejected" with a pointer to this one, etc.
